description: Hi ! We're a team of hackathon rookies.
summary: AstroMind is a web-based monitoring and	support system for astronaut mental and physical wellbeing.  It combines passive sensing (wearable vitals,	sleep,	cabin	environment,	voice features, proximity), active	check-ins (a short,	open-ended daily conversation	built on validated psychometric instruments) and context	(schedule,	workload, cabin	events). It will then convert them into one simple, explainable status for each crew member: Normal, Warning or Critical.

We have three role based experience : 

Astronaut (Personal tab) - One status card, readings grouped into Vitals, Mental state, Social, Sleep, and Cabin & safety, with 7 live vitals including hydration. Also a cabin remote, a sleep report that links each awakening to its environmental cause, and Rimau, the onboard AI assistant.

Astronaut (Team tab) - Each crewmate's overall status, a mock CCTV layout, shared plans and gentle "check in on..." nudges. Tapping a crewmate shows their physical metrics only.

Ground team (flight director / flight surgeon) - A supervision dashboard that answers three questions first: Who needs attention? Is anyone experiencing similar changes? What has changed since yesterday?

Our concept is to create a personal health and wellbeing copilot for astronauts, supported by a monitoring platform for their crew and ground-based medical personnel.

Instead of presenting large amounts of raw health data, AstroNomad focuses on three questions:

  • How am I doing? — Understand current health and wellbeing.
  • What has changed? — Identify unusual readings or concerning trends.
  • What should I do next? — Receive relevant guidance and follow-up recommendations.

The platform combines three approaches.

Personalised monitoring

Each astronaut's readings are compared with their individual pre-flight baseline. This helps identify changes that may be missed when using general population averages.

Context-aware assessment

The system considers factors such as workload, exercise, spacewalk preparation, sleep disruption and environmental conditions before interpreting unusual readings. This helps distinguish potentially expected changes from those requiring further investigation.

Guided support through Rimau

Rimau serves as an approachable AI-powered companion, helping astronauts understand their health information, complete daily psychological check-ins and access appropriate support.

AstroNomad also separates information according to user roles. Astronauts receive a simple personal dashboard, crewmates can check on one another without unrestricted access to private psychological information, and authorised ground personnel receive the information needed for health supervision.

Together, these features aim to turn complex health measurements into understandable insights and appropriate next steps.
